    If you’re late to the AI party, don’t worry. It’s easier than you think to start leveraging artificial intelligence tools in your marketing strategy. Here are 11 AI marketing tools every marketer should start using today.

    Industry observers note that personalize is an AI-powered technology that helps you identify and produce highly targeted sales and marketing campaigns by tracking the products and services your contacts are most interested in at any given time. The platform uses an algorithm to identify each contact’s top three interests, which are updated in real-time based on recent site activity.

    Recent findings suggest that seventh Sense provides behavioral analytics that helps you win attention in your customers’ overcrowded email inboxes. Choosing the best day and time to send an email is always a gamble. And while some days of the week generally get higher open rates than others, you’ll never be able to nail down a time that’s best for every customer. Seventh Sense eases your stress of having to figure out the perfect send-time and day for your email campaigns. The AI-based platform figures out the best timing and email frequency for each contact based on when they’re opening emails. The tool is primarily geared toward HubSpot and Marketo customers.

    Phrasee uses artificial intelligence to help you write more effective subject lines. With its AI-based Natural Language Generation system, Phrasee uses data-driven insights to generate millions of natural-sounding copy variants that match your brand voice. The model is end-to-end, meaning when you feed the results back to Phrasee, the prediction model rebuilds so it can continuously learn from your audience.

    According to recent reports, hubSpot Search Engine Optimization (SEO) is an integral tool for the Human Content team. It uses machine learning to determine how search engines understand and categorize your content. HubSpot SEO helps you improve your search engine rankings and outrank your competitors. Search engines reward websites that organize their content around core subjects, or topic clusters. HubSpot SEO helps you discover and rank for the topics that matter to your business and customers.

    When you’re limited to testing two variables against each other at a time, it can take months to get the results you’re looking for. Evolv AI lets you test all your ideas at once. It uses advanced algorithms to identify the top-performing concepts, combine them with each other, and repeat the process to achieve the best site experience.

    According to recent reports, acrolinx is a content alignment platform that helps brands scale and improves the quality of their content. It’s geared toward enterprises – its major customers include big brands like Google, Adobe, and Amazon - to help them scale their writing efforts. Instead of spending time chasing down and fixing typos in multiple places throughout an article or blog post, you can use Acrolinx to do it all right there in one place. You start by setting your preferences for style, grammar, tone of voice, and firm-specific word usage. Then, Acrolinx checks and scores your existing content to find what’s working and suggest areas for improvement. The platform provides real-time guidance and suggestions to make writing better and strengthen weak pages.

    According to recent reports, marketMuse uses an algorithm to help marketers build content strategies. The tool shows you where to target keywords to rank in specific topic categories, and recommends keywords you should go after if you want to own particular topics. It also identifies gaps and opportunities for latest content and prioritizes them by their probable impact on your rankings. The algorithm compares your content with thousands of articles related to the same topic to uncover what’s missing from your site.

    Copilot is a suite of tools that help eCommerce businesses maintain real-time communication with customers around the clock at every stage of the funnel. Promote products, recover shopping carts and send updates or reminders directly through Messenger.

    Recent findings suggest that yotpo’s deep learning technology evaluates your customers’ product reviews to help you make better business decisions. It identifies key topics that customers mention related to your products—and their feelings toward them. The AI engine extracts relevant reviews from past buyers and presents them in smart displays to convert newly introduced shoppers. Yotpo also saves you time moderating reviews. The AI-powered moderation tool automatically assigns a score to each review and flags reviews with negative sentiment so you can focus on quality control instead of manually reviewing every post.

    It has been revealed that albert is a self-learning software that automates the creation of marketing campaigns for your brand. It analyzes vast amounts of data to run optimized campaigns autonomously, allowing you to feed in your own creative content and target markets, and then use data from its database to determine key characteristics of a serious buyer. Albert identifies potential customers that match those traits, and runs trial campaigns on a small group of customers—with results refined by Albert himself—before launching it on a larger scale.

    Albert plugs into your existing marketing technology stack, so you still have access to your accounts, ads, search, social media, and more. Albert maps tracking and attribution to your source of truth so you can determine which channels are driving your business.

    There are many tools and companies out there that offer AI tools, but this is a small list of resources that we have found to be helpful. If you have any other suggestions, feel free to share them in the comments below this article. As marketing evolves at such a rapid pace, fresh marketing strategies will be invented that we haven't even dreamed of yet. But for now, this list should give you a good starting point on your way to implementing AI into your marketing mix.

    Mastering TypeScript Utility Types: Write Cleaner, Smarter Code

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (437 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dev

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • TypeScript utility types are built-in tools provided by the TypeScript language that allow developers to transform and manipulate existing data types into newly introduced ones without rewriting them from scratch.
    • Imagine you run a commercial bakery that specializes in custom wedding cakes.
    • TypeScript utility types work exactly like those sticky-note instructions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    TypeScript utility types are built-in tools provided by the TypeScript language that allow developers to transform and manipulate existing data types into newly introduced ones without rewriting them from scratch. Data types act as rigid blueprints describing what information a variable or object can hold in an application. By using utility types, developers can take a single standard blueprint and instantly create tailored variations—such as making certain properties optional or stripping out private fields—with minimal effort.

    Imagine you run a commercial bakery that specializes in custom wedding cakes. Instead of printing a completely newly introduced, multi-page master recipe book every single time a customer wants a minor modification—such as a chocolate cake without nuts or a vanilla cake with extra frosting—you keep one master reference recipe. When an order comes in, you attach a quick instruction sticky note to the master recipe: "Use the standard chocolate cake recipe, but make the nuts optional and omit the fruit filling.".

    TypeScript utility types work exactly like those sticky-note instructions. Instead of copying and pasting complex code blueprints to make slight changes, you apply a utility type to your master blueprint, telling TypeScript precisely how to adjust the requirements for a specific task.

    In real-world software engineering, application requirements change constantly. If developers maintain separate, duplicate blueprints for creating a user account, updating a user account, and displaying a public user profile, changing a single detail (like renaming an email field) requires manual updates across all those duplicate definitions.

    Engineers use utility types to establish a single source of truth for their data structures. This prevents subtle production bugs where an update API endpoint expects different data fields than the original record, saves hours of redundant maintenance, and ensures that changes made to core database models propagate automatically across backend services.

    It has been revealed that below is an example of an Express.js controller in a Node.js application. Notice how we define a single User blueprint, and then use built-in utility types like Omit and Partial to shape the input payloads for user registration and profile updates.

    Utility types are not just syntactical shortcuts; they are essential architectural tools that keep your data structures synchronized, maintainable, and DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself). By leveraging built-in helpers like Partial, Pick, and Omit, you eliminate duplicate interface definitions, drastically reduce maintenance overhead, and build resilient Node.js services that adapt gracefully as your software evolves.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It's hard to mess up a Reuben because the ingredients are so simple: corned beef, sliced thin, tangy sauerkraut, Swiss cheese, and Thousand Island dressing (or Russian), all of which are sandwiched between two pieces of sturdy rye bread.
    • To that end, Food Republic did the legwork and created a list of the top Reubens you can order from a chain, from customers' perspectives, and one of the entries actually comes from Culver's.
    • Were you aware that Culver's even had a Grilled Reuben Melt on its menu?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It's hard to mess up a Reuben because the ingredients are so simple: corned beef, sliced thin, tangy sauerkraut, Swiss cheese, and Thousand Island dressing (or Russian), all of which are sandwiched between two pieces of sturdy rye bread. No matter where you get your Reuben from, it's safe to say there are typically no bad ones — just good, better, and best.

    To that end, Food Republic did the legwork and created a list of the top Reubens you can order from a chain, from customers' perspectives, and one of the entries actually comes from Culver's. The Midwestern favorite, better known for its unique ButterBurgers, apparently makes the best grilled version of the sandwich you can find.

    Were you aware that Culver's even had a Grilled Reuben Melt on its menu? Because for as many customers who sing its praises, there appear to be an equal number who didn't even know it was an option. But what an option it is; it's a classic version, with lightly toasted bread, piles of salty corned beef, and melty Swiss cheese made in Culver's home state of Wisconsin.

    One Reddit user shouted out the sandwich, writing that it "matches or beats some of the ones that I've had at many diners." Another commenter remarked that Culver's "slaps in general[,] but this goes hard for a fast food Reuben." Meanwhile, yet another Redditor called it "the best thing on the menu and the best [Reuben] I've ever had.".

    One of the best things about Culver's menu is how customizable it is, and the Reuben is no different. Culver's maintains a fairly long list of toppings that you can add to your melt; one Reddit user claimed that "[grilled onions] and mushrooms are the easiest way to elevate the sandwiches," though keep in mind that you might have to request customizations in person because online ordering doesn't always have the option. You could also add raw onions for a sharper bite, lettuce for a little greenery, tomato for some extra umami flavor, and, for a small fee, some thick-cut bacon.

    Another user suggested adding a burger patty to the sandwich, calling the addition "incredible." Finally, if you're not a huge fan of rye, you could also swap it out for sourdough (the melt would then actually more closely resemble the best non-traditional chain restaurant Reuben, found at Schlotzsky's Deli), or opt for its Kaiser bun, brioche roll, gluten-free bun if you have a wheat allergy.

    12 Powdered Gravy Mixes, Ranked Worst To Best

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (3028 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways

    • Sources indicate that even so, the kind of store-bought gravy mix you choose matters — after all, anything you're planning to drown your meat and taters in had better be good.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    Recent findings suggest that as most pro home chefs will tell you, making gravy from scratch isn't exactly rocket science. With the help of a little flour, butter, and broth, you could be on your way to a delicious gravy in just a few minutes. Still, there may be times when you simply aren't feeling up to it — whether you've had a rough week or are drowning in to-dos, packets of powdered gravy mix can prove a simple, flavorful fix.

    Sources indicate that even so, the kind of store-bought gravy mix you choose matters — after all, anything you're planning to drown your meat and taters in had better be good. That's why I decided to make it my mission to test some of the most popular powdered gravy options in my area in hopes of offering my honest opinion about which truly deserves a spot in your kitchen.

    In the upcoming post, I'm giving a complete rundown of every store-bought powdered gravy mix I could find, including the pricing, size, and taste of each. Bear in mind that the details mentioned in this article are subject to change and that the gravy packet selection featured here may not be reflective of what's available in your area. With that, join me as I prepare, taste, and rank 12 store-bought powdered gravy mixes from worst to best.

    Prices are as of the date of publication and may vary based on region.

    Industry observers note that great Value Chicken Gravy Mix is a no-frills Walmart-branded product that is, surprisingly, one of the costlier options on the list when you consider its price per unit. Though tagged at only 92 cents per packet, each pack contains .87 ounces, meaning you'll pay roughly $1.06 per ounce of powdered gravy.

    It has been revealed that great Value Chicken Gravy Mix is prepared using the standard 1 cup of water per 1 packet of mix, and its ingredients include monosodium glutamate (otherwise known as "MSG"), which may pose a problem for gravy lovers who may be sensitive to the ingredient. I tore open the packet, and its unappetizing, artificial smell hit me right away. Once cooked, the mixture turned creamy and thick, but its color seemed unnatural, especially when compared to homemade. I gave it a hesitant taste, and nope, not good — Great Value Chicken Gravy Mix tasted like stale chicken and literally made me gag.

    Would I recommend purchasing Great Value Chicken Gravy Mix? No way. Not only does its bright yellow color not resemble any chicken gravy I've ever made, but the taste was barely tolerable. I'm sure you could try improving this store-bought gravy with Worcestershire sauce, but I say, if it's convenience you seek, there are other options more deserving of your coin than this one.

    Sources indicate that I hate to have to rank yet another Great Value powdered gravy mix so close to the bottom of the list, but it simply cannot be helped. Great Value Turkey Gravy Mix is a bit cheaper than its chicken-flavored counterpart — expect to pay 78 cents per .87 ounces, which works out to around 89.7 cents per ounce of powdered gravy. Great Value Turkey Gravy Mix doesn't contain the MSG that the chicken flavor includes, but that doesn't mean I recommend purchasing it — like the former, it has a weird smell and taste that I simply can't get past.

    According to recent reports, I prepared Great Value Turkey Gravy Mix according to the package directions and watched it bubble and simmer on the stove. The mix eventually turned the typical light brown color normally associated with turkey gravy and had an uber-thick consistency. I let it cool slightly before giving it a quick taste — sadly, it had the same stomach-churning qualities as the previous flavor. Great Value Turkey Gravy Mix tasted woefully artificial; in fact, the additives or chemicals present in the gravy were just about the only thing I could taste. Needless to say, I would never dish up Great Value Turkey Gravy Mix to guests at Thanksgiving — you'd be better off leaving not-so-Great Value picks like this one on the shelf.

    Before offering my opinion here, I have to be honest and say I'm not a person who prepares peppered gravy often. That noted, I'm willing to bet Southeastern Mills Peppered Gravy Mix doesn't quite encapsulate its classic flavor the way other options do.

    It has been revealed that southeastern Mills Peppered Gravy Mix costs $1.22 per 2.75 ounces, with a unit price of 44.4 cents per ounce. As is typical for many peppered gravy mixes on the market, this packet contains a little more powdered gravy mix per pack than other varieties and flavors. Its preparation requires more water, too — you'll need 1 ¾ cups this time around versus the usual 1 cup.

    Sources indicate that southeastern Mills Peppered Gravy Mix tasted annoyingly bland, with a flavor very similar to what you'd get if you added black pepper to plain cream. Though thick, it had no richness of flavor, and I couldn't imagine it doing much to elevate anyone's sausage gravy. I flipped the packet over and was surprised by what I saw on the ingredient list: Palm oil and modified food starch were the first ingredients mentioned, which is hardly a good way to start a high-quality gravy, if you ask me. As I mentioned, I am by no means an expert in peppered gravy, but based on first impressions alone, I'd say skip this brand and opt for other, richer, more flavorful brands on the market.

    If you're surprised to see McCormick Brown Gravy Mix ranked lower on the list, join the club. I, for one, adore brown gravy, and with McCormick being one of the most popular gravy and seasoning brands on the market, I figured I'd be in for a real treat. Expect to pay 97 cents for .87 ounces of it, making each ounce cost roughly $1.12.

    According to recent reports, when cooking up McCormick Brown Gravy Mix, I couldn't help but feel excited — its texture was thick and glossy, and the gravy had a deep brown hue that just screamed umami beef. It even had the savory, enticing aroma of a succulent pot roast, so imagine my surprise when I discovered the gravy tastes, quite literally, like nothing.

    In a recent development, that's right — McCormick Brown Gravy Mix features a flavor so weak I could barely taste anything at all. To think McCormick Brown Gravy Mix smelled and looked so great without delivering flavor even half of what was teased is mind-boggling. Needless to say, McCormick Brown Gravy Mix isn't worth the buy — I'd recommend picking up some beef broth and making your own simple brown gravy or choosing one of the higher-ranking varieties over this one.

    Though not the best out there, Amazon Grocery Brown Gravy Mix is a dark horse in terms of taste and performance. The gravy comes sold in an .87-ounce pack and was priced at 83 cents, about 95 cents per ounce. It contains artificial ingredients along with a host of additives, but hey, if that kinda stuff doesn't bother you, feel free to ignore those stats.

    Industry observers note that I went into my tasting of Amazon Grocery Brown Gravy Mix with low expectations — almost every Amazon Grocery item I've sampled in the past left me underwhelmed. Much to my amazement, Amazon Grocery Brown Gravy Mix held its own in terms of consistency and aroma — it was a bit thinner than a few other options on the list, yes, but still managed to be just thick enough. I also found its glossy deep brown appearance mesmerizing, and its smell rich and meaty, just the way a good brown gravy should be.

    Going in for a slurp, I didn't walk away disappointed — though the flavor was nowhere near as potent as its aroma, it was leaps and bounds better than McCormick. I could clearly taste its beefy notes, and its umami depth was decent overall. One thing I will say is that Amazon Grocery Brown Gravy Mix tastes slightly watered down; still, I think it will get you by if you're looking for a tasty, inexpensive brown gravy to crown your mashers.

    Industry observers note that pioneer Peppered Gravy Mix is pretty good; though not a peppered gravy kinda gal, I have an appreciation for this brand and would recommend it over Southeastern Mills any day. This mix comes in a 2.75-ounce packet, only this time, you'll need to add 2 cups of water instead of the 1 ¾ cups Southeastern Mills requires. Each packet costs $1.33, meaning you'll cop this powdered peppered gravy for about 48.4 cents per ounce.

    When cooking up Pioneer Peppered Gravy Mix, the first thing I noticed was its golden hue. The yellowish tinge of the Pioneer-branded gravy made it more attractive than the stark white presentation of Southeastern Mills. It was just as thick as the former brand, if not thicker, though whether or not its flavor would prove better was yet to be seen.

    Sources indicate that so, how'd Pioneer Peppered Gravy Mix taste? Though I still consider its flavor mundane compared to traditional chicken or brown gravies, Pioneer Peppered Gravy Mix had more depth than Southeastern Mills. It's not listed in the ingredients, but there seemed to be a hint of butter flavor in the mixture — this deepened the taste and added complexity. All in all, if I were to grab a packet of peppered gravy for breakfast, this is the brand I'd get — not only does it look better, but its taste is pretty decent, too.

    Recent findings suggest that mcCormick Turkey Gravy Seasoning Mix wasn't too bad — it isn't something I'd choose over homemade gravy for Thanksgiving dinner, but it's good if you're in a pinch and want something cheap. The gravy comes sold in a .87-ounce packet for $1.63, and while this might not sound super expensive, it's actually a little pricier than others, at $1.87 per ounce.

    It has been revealed that mcCormick Turkey Gravy Seasoning Mix yields a light brown color I found fitting for turkey gravy — it certainly looked the part, featuring a medium-thick consistency and glossy appearance. McCormick Turkey Gravy Seasoning Mix has a poultry-like flavor that's pleasing but leans more chicken than turkey in my opinion. Nevertheless, I consider this turkey gravy option to be one of the punchier, more robust picks out there, and though I don't necessarily consider it holiday worthy, it might be good to have a packet or two in your pantry for days when you're low on time.

    Recent findings suggest that fire & Smoke Society Big Sunday Brown Gravy Mix is a super unique option, and though I probably wouldn't buy it again, you might consider trying it if you're looking to sample something outside of the norm. The packaging here has the kind of aesthetic that makes you think it's fancy by looks alone — its price also stands out, at $1.72 per 1-ounce pack, working out to $1.72 per ounce. A quick scan of the ingredients reveals several surprises — though not a clean ingredient pick by any means, some additions — like cumin, chili powder, and even coffee — left me curious as to what kind of flavor I was in for.

    I prepared the gravy as per its 1 cup to 1 packet instructions and immediately noticed a difference in its texture compared to the others. Fire & Smoke Society Major Sunday Brown Gravy Mix yields a thinner, silkier texture than most. Its aroma was totally unexpected, as it was more akin to grill spices than savory beef. After tasting Fire & Smoke Society's Big Sunday Brown Gravy Mix, I found myself torn — the taste wasn't gross, but didn't encompass the type of flavor I expect from a classic brown gravy.

    Recent findings suggest that is Fire & Smoke Society Major Sunday Brown Gravy Mix good? Yes! Would I buy it again? Probably not. Blame it on my traditional taste buds, but for me, this powdered gravy mix is just OK.

    Is there a difference between country and peppered gravy? Apparently, there is, and as it stands, I prefer the former. Kinder's Classic Country Gravy Dry Seasoning was a breath of fresh air flavor-wise, but I suppose that isn't surprising given I love practically anything that the Kinder brand produces. Kinder's Classic Country Gravy Dry Seasoning was priced at $1.72 per 1.9 ounces at my local Walmart, working out to about 90.5 cents per ounce.

    Kinder's Classic Country Gravy Dry Seasoning was truly phenomenal in terms of taste and texture. First and foremost, the gravy recommends preparing it with 2 cups of milk, which automatically gave it a richer, sweeter finish. Once cooked, the gravy was thick and featured a stark white appearance flecked with tons of contrasting black pepper throughout.

    Kinder's Classic Country Gravy Dry Seasoning tastes almost identical to creamy, buttery, garlicky mashed potatoes, no spuds needed. I'd imagine this would taste incredible paired with creamy taters, and I wouldn't hesitate to dish it up as a turkey topper during the holidays. As if things couldn't get better, Kinder's Classic Country Gravy Dry Seasoning uses fairly clean ingredients, with nowhere near as much of the ick featured in other powdered gravy mixes on the list. With all things considered, Kinder's Classic Country Gravy Dry Seasoning is one of my favorite powdered gravy mixes on the market.

    Sources indicate that simply Organic Roasted Chicken Gravy Seasoning Mix costs $1.72 for .85 ounces making it one of the most expensive powdered gravy mixes on the market at $2.02 per ounce. It's the only gluten-free organic chicken option on the list, and I honestly didn't expect it to taste as good as it did. Not that I have anything against organic foods — I actually love them and find the use of minimal ingredients refreshing. Still, in the world of gravy, I guess I just didn't expect a natural option like this one to hold its own when pitted against others containing various flavor-boosting additives. Thankfully, this humble pick from Simply Organic proved me wrong.

    It has been revealed that simply Organic chicken gravy calls for the standard 1 cup of gravy packet seasoning per 1 cup of water. As it cooked, it began to take on a sauce-like consistency that was thick, glossy, and light brown. I gave it a taste and was floored — this organic pick boasted a flavor way better than any other store-bought chicken gravy I've tried.

    Recent findings suggest that simply Organic chicken gravy had a bold, savory, and garlicky flavor beautifully enhanced with prominent notes of celery seed. Thus, though expensive, you can rest assured that your money is going to good use — Simply Organic Roasted Chicken Gravy Seasoning Mix is a phenomenal replacement for homemade when you don't feel like whipping up chicken gravy on your own.

    Sources indicate that simply Organic Brown Gravy Seasoning Mix is the only organic brown gravy on the list, and let me tell you, it did not disappoint. Unlike its chicken-flavored predecessor, Simply Organic Brown Gravy Seasoning Mix is slightly cheaper, at 1 ounce for $1.72 ( $1.72 per ounce). Being the organic grab that it is, expect Simply Organic brown gravy to be non-GMO and free of artificial colors, flavors, and ingredients. One of its best attributes is its use of cornstarch rather than flour, as this makes it a great option for people looking to ditch wheat.

    Sources indicate that I was delighted to find Simply Organic Brown Gravy Seasoning Mix packing so much flavor — after the previous brown gravy duds, I didn't have much hope that there was a truly good packaged option out there. In truth, Simply Organic's brown gravy is one of the most flavorful in its class — it was one of the few to truly capture the beefy, oniony savor I come to expect from a good homemade brown gravy.

    It has been revealed that one thing to note is that Simply Organic brown gravy has a medium consistency and a color a lot lighter than others in its category. Still, Simply Organic Brown Gravy Seasoning Mix would make the perfect companion to roast beef or over creamy mashed potatoes, and I doubt anyone would be able to detect the difference between it and homemade.

    According to recent reports, yellowstone Jalapeño Gravy is unlike any other gravy I've tried — I had never sampled jalapeño gravy before, nor did I know it existed. Now that it's on my radar, in my cabinet it will stay. It's really that good, even if it is $2.50 per 2.82-ounce packet (89 cents per ounce)!

    Recent findings suggest that yellowstone Jalapeño Gravy contains no artificial flavors, which to me is pretty impressive. Though not gluten-free like the aforementioned Simply Organic picks, it does at least contain fewer additives while still managing to achieve unbelievably thick results. You only need to use 2 cups of water per packet to cash in on this irresistibly luscious golden gravy; its texture was so rich and smooth my mouth watered just at the sight of it.

    Aside from its tantalizing consistency, Yellowstone Jalapeño Gravy tastes incredible — I'd describe its flavor as similar to high-quality jalapeño nacho cheese, but with less emphasis on the cheese. It's quite spicy, and though not unbearably so, still isn't something I'd recommend offering to kids. All in all, Yellowstone Jalapeño Gravy is an amazing option I'd buy over and over again — try it on fried chicken cutlets, potatoes, stuffing, or hot sandwiches. Yum!

    Sources indicate that the 12 powdered gravy mixes selected for this article were chosen based on availability in my area, with most sourced from Walmart and Amazon. Each gravy mix was ranked primarily based on texture and flavor, although other factors, like ingredients and pricing, were considered. As always, pricing and availability are subject to change.

    Industry observers note that chatGPT is a large language model that generates human-like responses to a variety of prompts. It can be used for tasks such as language translation, question answering, and text completion. It can handle a wide range of topics and styles of writing, and generates coherent and fluent text, but should be used with care as it may generate text that is biased, offensive, or factually incorrect.

    Overall, ChatGPT is a powerful tool for natural language processing, but it should be used with care and with an understanding of its limitations.

    Industry observers note that DALL-E is a generative model developed by OpenAI that is capable of generating images from text prompts. It is based on the GPT-3 architecture, which is a transformer-based neural network language model that has been trained on a massive dataset of text. DALL-E can generate images that are similar to a training dataset and it can generate high-resolution images that are suitable for commercial use.

    Industry observers note that overall, DALL-E is a powerful AI-based tool for generating images, it can be used for a variety of applications such as creating images for commercial use, gaming, and other creative projects. It is notable to note that the generated images should be reviewed and used with care, as they may not be entirely original and could be influenced by the training data.

    Sources indicate that lumen5 is a content creation platform that uses AI to help consumers create videos, social media posts, and other types of content. It has several features that make it useful for content creation and marketing, including:.

    Grammarly is a writing-enhancement platform that uses AI to check for grammar, punctuation, and spelling errors in the text.     Industry observers note that openAI Codex is a system developed by OpenAI that can create code from natural language descriptions of software tasks. The system is based on the GPT-3 model and can generate code in multiple programming languages.

However, the quality of the generated code may vary depending on the task description and it is vital to review and test the code before using it in a production environment. It is important to use the tool as an aid, not a replacement for the developer's knowledge.

    In a recent development, tabnine is a code completion tool that uses AI to predict and suggest code snippets. It is compatible with multiple programming languages and can be integrated with various code editors.

    Overall, TabNine is a useful tool for developers that can help improve coding efficiency and reduce the time spent on writing code. However, it is crucial to review the suggestions provided by the tool and use them with caution, as they may not always be accurate or appropriate. It is important to use the tool as an aid, not a replacement for the developer's knowledge.

    Jasper is a content writing and content generation tool that uses artificial intelligence to identify the best words and sentences for your writing style and medium in the most efficient, quick, and accessible way.

    It has been revealed that surfer SEO is a software tool designed to help website owners and digital marketers improve their search engine optimization (SEO) efforts. The tool provides a variety of features that can be used to analyze a website's on-page SEO, including:.

However, it is important to remember that it is just a tool and should be used in conjunction with other SEO best practices. Additionally, the tool is not a guarantee of better ranking.

    It has been revealed that zapier is a web automation tool that allows owners to automate repetitive tasks by connecting different web applications together. It does this by creating "Zaps" that automatically move data between apps, and can also be used to trigger certain actions in one app based on events in another app.

    Sources indicate that overall, Zapier is a useful tool that can help users automate repetitive tasks and improve workflow.     12 Costco Cakes You Should Be Picking Up In November 2026

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    From birthdays to holiday gatherings, a beautiful cake can be the star attraction and make an ordinary occasion feel extraordinary. Thanksgiving is right around the corner, and while pies are often the go-to dessert for this holiday, serving your guests something unexpected in the form of a cake can turn your dinner into a memorable feast, especially if they have multiple meals to attend. Sure, you can make one from scratch, but with all the activity and planning surrounding this holiday, you may just want to opt for something store-bought, and Costco offers the perfect solution.

    The Costco bakery offers a huge range, from decadent layer cakes in crowd-pleasing flavors to rich cheesecakes — which aren't technically cakes, though we're including them here anyway. There are also some Italian-style specialties, a truly seasonal option, and one flourless chocolate cake that will bring a touch of luxury to your table.

    According to recent reports, keep in mind that the wholesale club requires a membership for customers to shop there. If you're not already a member, this list of cakes may convince you to join. Just remember that prices and availability may vary by location and that some cakes may only be available to order online.

    Sources indicate that when it comes to Thanksgiving, few people would argue with the idea that the holiday isn't complete without at least one pumpkin dessert. However, instead of serving the expected pie this year, opt for this cheesecake — in addition to a creamy base full of intense pumpkin flavor, the whole dessert is topped with pecans and a generous drizzle of caramel sauce.

    A two-pack of Ferrara's Bakery 8-inch Pumpkin Cheesecake with Caramel and Pecan Topping is available at Costco for $119.99.

    Panettone is an Italian delicacy made from a yeasted dough studded with dried and candied fruit, and it has a lightly sweet flavor and fluffy texture. This bready cake is incredibly versatile and can be the foundation for many fall recipes. Try tearing it into pieces to make a delicious bread pudding, or follow Giada De Laurentiis's suggestion for leftover panettone and use it to top a holiday salad.

    Chiostro di Saronno Panettone Classico is available at Costco for $29.99.

    In a recent development, whether you're starting your day with a cup of joe, pausing for a midafternoon pick-me-up, or finishing a meal with coffee or tea, this cake from Collin Street Bakery should be on the table. It comes in a beautiful white tin and includes a cup of icing for drizzling, while the warming cinnamon spice feels like a hug on your palate. It also makes a beautiful gift.

    Collin Street Bakery Cinnamon Coffee Cake is available at Costco for $34.99.

    Collin Street Bakery is a Texas-based organization, and the Lone Star State is known for producing pecans, so you're almost guaranteed to have delicious pecan flavor in this pair of cakes. Besides containing the rich nuts, each one is chock-full of either pineapple or glacéed apricots. The batter for these cakes is also sweetened with honey.

    Collin Street Bakery Apricot & Pineapple Pecan Cake Bundle is available at Costco for $64.99.

    For some, Christmas cannot arrive soon enough. Fortunately, Costco has a little preview of the holiday for these individuals in the form of this mini pecan cake bundle, which includes four favorite flavors: cherry fudge cake, pineapple cake, blonde cake, and a classic fruitcake. If you're wondering how fruitcakes can last all year, adding a heavy dose of alcohol can help preserve them.

    The Collin Street Bakery Mini Pecan Cake Bundle is available at Costco for $49.99.

    According to recent reports, the Knipschildt brand once held the Guinness World Record for the most expensive chocolate truffle in the world, but you don't need to take out a loan to enjoy this dessert. This flourless cake features a layer of rich chocolate ganache and is finished with the chocolatier's signature truffles. It's a striking cake that will bring a bit of sophistication to your next gathering.

    Knipschildt Chocopologie Truffle Flourless Chocolate Cake is available at Costco for $69.99.

    According to recent reports, tiramisu may seem like tres leches, but it's an entirely different dessert. Its name translates to "lift me up," and while traditional versions may come in a square format, this one from Ferrara's Bakery is round and features an attractive collar of brown and white stripes. The bakery makes its own ladyfingers and douses them in coffee and coffee liqueur before layering them with sweetened mascarpone cheese.

    A two-pack of Ferrara's Bakery 8-inch Tiramisu Cake is available at Costco for $99.99.

    If you love the combination of chocolate and peanut butter, then this cake is for you. The base is made from a fudge brownie, and it's topped with layers of peanut butter mousse and decadent chocolate cake. As if that's not enough, the whole confection gets a crown of brownie pieces, chocolate fudge, and peanut butter chips.

    For the consummate chocolate lover, no other flavors should get in the way of a chocolate cake, and this one is nothing short of perfection. It starts with four layers of rich chocolate sponge sandwiching velvety milk chocolate mousse; then, the entire thing gets covered in chocolate ganache and a coating of chocolate shavings that resemble bark, making this cake look like an edible tree trunk. It's pre-sliced, too, ensuring that everyone gets a fair share.

    It has been revealed that sometimes simple is better, especially when you want to add your own personal touches to something, and this plain Jon Donaire cheesecake is a perfect example. Try drizzling it with dulce de leche and finishing it with chopped walnuts, or top it with apple pie filling and a sprinkling of mixed spices for an autumnal take on a classic. You can even cover it with poached pear halves.

    Jon Donaire 10-inch Latest York Cheesecake is available at Costco for $59.99.

    This carrot cake features thick layers of cake and cream cheese frosting and is covered with a generous coating of vanilla buttercream. For an elegant touch, it's topped with silk cherry blossoms, and comes in a striking box tied with a beautiful ribbon, too. If you're not a fan of nuts or raisins, this cake is free of both, so nothing gets in the way of the spiced carrot flavor.

    The Cake Bake Shop 8-inch Round Carrot Cake is available at Costco for $159.99.

    The Egg McMuffin Order You Can Only Find In Canada

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • McDonald's breakfast is a thing of beauty, and if you think we've got it good here in the States, you probably haven't seen what's sitting on Canada's breakfast menu.
    • The Egg BLT starts with McDonald's signature ring-shaped steamed (not fried) egg, paired with hickory-smoked bacon, crisp lettuce, and fresh tomato, then finished with a creamy, mayo-like sauce and a slice of cheese, all stacked on a toasted English muffin.
    • Sources indicate that to get your hands on an Egg BLT McMuffin in the U.S., you'll have to get creative.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    McDonald's breakfast is a thing of beauty, and if you think we've got it good here in the States, you probably haven't seen what's sitting on Canada's breakfast menu. Alongside familiar faves, you'll find items Americans can't order, the most envy-inducing among them arguably being the Egg BLT McMuffin. Once you hear what's in it, don't be surprised if you catch yourself planning a trip to our northern neighbor.

    The Egg BLT starts with McDonald's signature ring-shaped steamed (not fried) egg, paired with hickory-smoked bacon, crisp lettuce, and fresh tomato, then finished with a creamy, mayo-like sauce and a slice of cheese, all stacked on a toasted English muffin. A second version uses nearly identical ingredients but swaps the whole leaves for shredded lettuce. You can only get this variation at McDonald's restaurants located inside Walmart stores — part of a decades-old partnership that once placed roughly 1,000 outposts in the retail chain. McDonald's later closed hundreds of them as drive-thrus became the main source of sales, though Walmart continues to host many locations in Canada.

    Sources indicate that to get your hands on an Egg BLT McMuffin in the U.S., you'll have to get creative. Your best bet is to start with a Bacon, Egg & Cheese McMuffin, which already ticks off half the ingredients. Ask for a touch of mayo, which gets you close to the sauce of the Canadian original. Since lettuce and tomatoes are lunchtime items, your odds improve near the end of breakfast hours when stores are prepping the lunch menu — you'll likely have to order them at the counter or window.

    It has been revealed that the Egg BLT might have already convinced you to add McDonald's to your itinerary next time you're in Canada, but it's not the only breakfast item worth the detour. One that caught our eye was the Mighty McGriddles. While the U.S. offers the Bacon, Egg & Cheese and Sausage, Egg & Cheese varieties separately, the Canadian version puts both to shame by stacking a double helping of hickory-smoked bacon, a sausage patty, egg, and cheese between two maple-flavored griddle cakes — a gloriously overstuffed creation that lives up to its name. The Mighty McMuffin follows the same logic, coming loaded with both meats for anyone who can never decide between the two.

    Another familiar face on Canadian McDonald's breakfast menus is the bagel, though while America only offers plain, Canada also serves sesame and everything varieties. You can even order one toasted with butter or Philadelphia cream cheese — widely known as the best store-bought brand — as if you're at a proper bagel shop.

    Recent findings suggest that canada's McDonald's restaurants aren't afraid to put a twist on U.S. staples, and they also introduce fresh items altogether. You won't find chicken anywhere on the standard U.S. breakfast menu, which makes the Chicken McGriddles feel like a curveball up north. The simple yet delicious sandwich pairs a breaded chicken patty with two sweet, maple-flavored griddle cakes for some serious sweet-and-savory fusion.

    #115070. 14 French Desserts You Should Try Once In Your Life

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2414 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    14 French Desserts You Should Try Once In Your Life

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2414 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, french cuisine is largely known for its decadent textures, flavors, and presentations, and this includes a long list of regional desserts.
    • According to recent reports, if you aren't already familiar with French desserts, it doesn't matter if you are fluent in the language or not; the names of the country's culinary creations don't always alert you to what they actually are.
    • The tart Tatin may have a fancy name, but don't let that fool you.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, french cuisine is largely known for its decadent textures, flavors, and presentations, and this includes a long list of regional desserts. We all know about croissants, and, yes, when infused with the right sweet elements, they definitely count as a dessert, but that's just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to French desserts. In fact, there is a seemingly never-ending list of eye-catching sweet treats that hail from the country. The ones found below, though, are so mouthwateringly delicious that everyone should try them at least once in their lives.

    According to recent reports, if you aren't already familiar with French desserts, it doesn't matter if you are fluent in the language or not; the names of the country's culinary creations don't always alert you to what they actually are. With this in mind, if you're interested in sampling a few — why wouldn't you be? — but aren't sure where to start, we can help point you in the right direction. So, get your fork and spoon ready, because once you learn about the collection of French desserts below, you'll be dying to get your hands on them.

    The tart Tatin may have a fancy name, but don't let that fool you. It is actually akin to an apple pie, just flipped upside down — and there's nothing extravagant about that. The French version of the dessert also has humble origins. As the story goes, in the late 1800s, Caroline (of Caroline and Stephanie Tatin's Inn, located south of Paris) forgot to put a crust on the bottom of her apple pie. Due to being exceptionally busy, she decided to put it on top instead and see what would happen. When she took it out of the oven and flipped it over, she saw that her misstep led to a happy result: The apples were beautifully caramelized. When she served it to the inn's guests, it was an immediate success, and the tarte Tatin was officially born.

    Creating a tart Tatin is fairly accessible to novice home cooks. It only calls for five ingredients: apples, flour, butter, eggs, and sugar. The trickiest part is arranging the slices of fruit in a decorative way on the bottom of the pan. Actually, despite her massive culinary repertoire, Ina Garten admits it is the recipe she makes most because it is not only delicious, but easy to create, as well. If it's good enough for Garten to come back time and time again, you'd better believe it's a French dessert everyone should give a go at least once.

    Sources indicate that crème brûlée is one of the most easily recognizable and widely popular French desserts in the United States, but, interestingly enough, its origins are somewhat disputed. France, England, and Spain all claim to be the birthplace of the dessert. Regardless, since its invention, wherever that happened to be, there's no doubt it has fully integrated itself into traditional French cuisine, and if you've never had the joy of eating one before, you are truly missing out.

    In a recent development, in its most basic format, crème brûlée is made with just four ingredients: egg yolks, sugar, heavy cream, and vanilla bean. While simple, the elements come together to form a creamy, custardy delight. Then, the top is scorched to form a layer of burnt sugar that's to die for. Topping it with a couple of fresh berries is also customary, but either way, it is simplicity at its finest. In fact, this is one case where the sum is much greater than its parts. In addition to the sweet, rich flavor of the custard itself, part of the fun of eating one is using a spoon to crack the burnt layer on top. It not only adds a caramelized taste but contributes textural variation, and that is always a plus. Whether you decide to try your hand at making crème brûlée yourself or choose to seek it out from a restaurant, it's a French dessert that's worth your attention.

    Éclairs have been around since the 1860s, and today, they are one of the more popular French desserts found in the United States. For good reason, too; they are tasty enough to go down in a flash. Speaking of which, the word directly translates to lightning.

    Name and popularity aside, éclairs are made with choux pastry, which is similar to doughnut pastry, but devoid of baking soda, baking powder, and yeast, and relies on steam to rise. As a result, after being formed into long cylindrical pieces, the dough cooks up to be exceptionally light and airy. That's just the start of the legendary éclair, though. They are also filled with pastry cream or custard and then topped with either fondant or ganache icing — both of which are harder styles of icing, so you can still feel free to enjoy éclairs with your hands.

    Industry observers note that arguably, the most popular flavor of éclair is chocolate, but thanks to the versatility of the choux pastry shell, they are welcoming to a world of other flavors as well. Everything from caramel to pistachio to Nutella to strawberry to matcha with chocolate and beyond can be found enhancing the delightful little pastry.

    French yogurt cake, or gâteaux au yaourt in the native language, is another easy yet extremely satisfying dessert that deserves some time in the spotlight. In France, it is a popular recipe for kids to learn, likely because of the simple recipe, which calls for three eggs, one part oil, one part yogurt, two parts sugar, three parts flour, and leavening. Even so, when it comes out of the oven, you have a drool-worthy, slightly tangy cake that is moister than pound cake (if you can fathom that) while still presenting a delicate crumb.

    Since French yogurt cake is not a common restaurant offering, if you want to give it a taste, you'll likely have to make one yourself. Or, at the very least, enlist a friend to do it — um, mom? Thankfully, though, it is one of the more straightforward must-try French desserts out there, so it should be attainable for even the most novice home cooks. The simplicity of the French yogurt cake also makes it prime for a plethora of flavor infusions. So, if you want to add citrus, or brandy, or fruit to the mix, go right ahead.

    It has been revealed that crêpes are a delicately thin pancake-like creation that's ready and waiting for a world of flavor and ingredient infusions. Still, a Crêpes Suzette is quite possibly the most delicious and famous version of them all. It consists of classic crêpes in a sauce made of sugar, orange juice, and an orange liqueur, like Gran Marnier. The entire thing is also smothered in brandy and set on fire, which leads to a caramelized, citrusy, sweet flambé sauce that will draw just about anyone in. Heck, even watching a chef prepare one catches the eye, and that's why it's often done in full view when ordered in a restaurant.

    Interestingly enough, crêpes Suzette is another iconic French dessert that was first created by accident — and this particular story is not disputed. In 1895, Henri Carpentier, a 14-year-old assistant waiter at the Maitre at Monte Carlo's Cafe Paris, was preparing dessert for the Prince of Wales (who'd later become King Edward VII of England). While doing so, he accidentally caught the cordials he was working with on fire, and instead of becoming flustered and starting over from scratch, he tasted the sauce and realized he'd come up with something extraordinary.

    Recent findings suggest that don't let the flambé scare you too much if you want to try creating one at home; it truly does lead to exceptional flavor. However, you can still make a tasty rendition sans the potential fire hazard; it just won't be quite as authentic.

    Industry observers note that first and foremost, Mont Blanc is known for being the highest mountain in the Alps. However, for those in the know, it is also a delectable French sweet treat with Alpine-inspired appeal. In fact, when created, the Mont Blanc dessert resembles a snow-capped mountain peak, so the name is more than fitting. The exact origins of it is uncertain, but a reigning theory is that it was developed in Paris, France, in the 19th century. During that era, chestnuts started to grow in popularity in the region, and people began incorporating them into sweet dishes, instead of the customary savory ones.

    The main components of a Mont Blanc dessert are as follows: It starts with a crisp meringue base, which is topped with thin strands of chestnut purée, and then finished off with a pile of whipped cream. Traditionally, a vermicelli tip is used to pipe the chestnut puree, but other shapes are also common. Either way, though, the yummy chestnut puree is the star of the show, offering a nutty, rich flavor that offsets the creamy whipped cream and meringue in a delightful way.

    Industry observers note that hailing from the Basque region in southwest France, the Gâteau Basque became widely popular in the 19th century. Its growth in the culinary scene is largely attributed to a particular baker, Marianne Hirigoyen, who first sold them in local markets before opening a brick-and-mortar bakery. Since then, the gâteau Basque's acceptance into French culinary tradition has been more than cemented. Actually, fast-forward to today, and there's now a museum and a two-day festival in October dedicated to the dessert. If that doesn't tell you exactly why it is a must-try French recipe, we don't know what would.

    Recent findings suggest that whether you call them canelé, cannelé de Bordeaux, or canelé Bordelais, these yummy little French pastries are time-consuming to make — the dough needs to rest for up to 24 hours before baking. Even so, their delectable mix of textures and delicious buttery, custard-y flavors are worth the effort used to make them and then some.

    Small and cylindrical with fluted edges, the center of canelés are made with flour, milk, sugar, butter, vanilla bean, eggs, salt, and rum. Once mixed with care, the dough rests for an extended time before baking in copper molds. After they're cooked, a delicious coating of edible beeswax and butter fills the molds and is also poured over the top before baking again. When that's done, you're left with delicious bite-sized (well, almost) custard-filled cakes featuring a caramelized crust on the exterior. Considering miniature copper fluted molds are not a customary tool in most homes, canelés aren't the first dessert we recommend trying to make at home. However, if you ever see them in a French bakery or restaurant, you'd be a fool not to give them a try.

    Opera cake is one of the coffee desserts that are always worth ordering, and guess what? It's also a French dessert everyone should try at least once. That is, of course, if you know what's good for you — and in this case, we truly hope you do.

    Created by Cyrique Gavillon, the opera cake is just as much a thing of beauty as it is a delectable flavor wonderland. A rectangular-shaped cake at heart, it is made with alternating layers of coffee syrup-soaked almond cake, buttercream, and ganache, and then topped with a rich dark chocolate icing. Once completed, it not only looks stunning, but provides your palate with a mix of nutty, chocolatey, creamy, rich, coffee flavors that are hard to beat. Yes, it sounds a whole lot like tiramisu when the elements are taken at face value, but it is a delightful dessert all its own when it comes to how the ingredients come together. Plus, it's French, not Italian. Just saying.

    Industry observers note that while simple to make, the Île flottante presents itself as an elegant dish, and as such, is a mainstay in French cuisine. In fact, while it's stated French people prefer to purchase dessert from a local bakery, it is one recipe many natives still have in their repertoire. It just so happened to be Julia Child's favorite old-school dessert, as well. Since she is credited with bringing French cuisine to the United States and helping it grow in popularity, following her lead regarding the greatest culinary hits of the country just makes sense.

    Similar to éclairs, which we've already discussed, profiteroles are made with hollowed-out choux pastry, filled with custard or cream, and topped with icing. What sets them apart is their shape. Instead of being long and cylindrical, profiteroles are formed into small bite-sized balls. As a result, they are the perfect sweet treat for bringing to a gathering or munching on if you simply want a few bites. However, once you get a taste of their scrumptious textures and flavors, trying to eat just one will be quite a complicated task.

    Again, like éclairs, the most common icing flavor for profiteroles is chocolate. Still, they come in a myriad of other flavors, as well, so they have what it takes to pique the interest of many. For example, if chocolate is too one-dimensional for you — we are judging you — you can also make chocolate hazelnut profiteroles, vanilla ones, or just about any other flavor you can dream up.

    Recent findings suggest that last but certainly not least on our list of French desserts you need to try is clafoutis. The name may sound posh, but it's actually another sweet treat that's incredibly easy to make, so you don't have to be an established French baker to create one at home. Plus, it may be a dessert, but it is also acceptable to eat it for breakfast. Okay, now we are really listening.

    Recent findings suggest that clafoutis consists of fruit smothered with a thick custard made from sugar, flour, milk, and eggs. The texture is akin to flan, but undeniably has all the French flair a Francophile could want. Most traditionally, cherries create the meaty fruit of clafoutis, but other berries and fruits, like raspberries, are also commonly used to pull off the recipe. While not necessarily a dessert, if you want to go in a savory direction, fruit can also be substituted for prosciutto, cheese, and tomatoes, so think of it like a choose-your-own-adventure type dish. No matter how you build it, though, clafoutis is one French creation that deserves more recognition, at least in the States.

    Looking to level up your content creation game in 2025? You're in the right place! The digital landscape has evolved dramatically, and AI tools have become essential for creators who want to stay ahead of the curve. In this guide, I'll show you the top 10 AI tools that are revolutionizing content creation and making creators' lives easier.

    Why You Need These AI Tools in 2025.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • Duck fat is one of the most prized cooking fats in the culinary world because it has a higher smoke point than butter (around 375 degrees Fahrenheit) and a beautifully silky texture rich in subtle, meaty flavors.
    • It has been revealed that using duck fat on grilled cheese is pretty easy, but there are a few tricks that can really maximize your results.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that A grilled cheese is already plenty hearty, but the common tip of using cured meats to increase its satisfying flavor — like in this tasty maple bacon variation — may interfere with your filling's texture if you prefer a smooth, gooey filling. Duck fat is the perfect way around this because it adds meatiness without changing any other ingredients, enriching the bread with umami with just a single smear.

    Duck fat is one of the most prized cooking fats in the culinary world because it has a higher smoke point than butter (around 375 degrees Fahrenheit) and a beautifully silky texture rich in subtle, meaty flavors. Just like spreading it on burger buns, using duck fat on grilled cheese can give you crispier bread because you can cook it at a higher temperature. When left at room temperature, it has a consistency similar to softened butter, making it easy to spread or drop in a pan, depending on your preference. Its unique composition of fats and subtle meaty flavor mean you'll notice its richness even in small amounts. Though it has a touch of gaminess, it's quite subtle and serves to elevate creamy and aged cheeses alike with an added layer of complexity.

    It has been revealed that using duck fat on grilled cheese is pretty easy, but there are a few tricks that can really maximize your results. Blending it with another fat, using it for some added seasoning, and picking the right pan can all give you the perfect sandwich.

    Mixing a fat with a high smoke point with one that burns more easily is a simple way to combine the best of both worlds. The richness of butter is irreplaceable, but you can incorporate some of duck fat's higher-heat cooking properties by swirling the two together before spreading the mix on your bread. Similarly, you can also bring your duck fat to a low, gentle simmer and add herbs and aromatics to flavor it beforehand. Whether you do this when rendering the fat yourself or just for a few minutes before adding your sandwich, a bit of sage can lend tremendous depth, while a smashed clove of garlic can mimic the rich flavor of toum.

    While a nonstick pan is great for butter since it doesn't retain as much heat, you might want to go in the opposite direction for duck fat. A heavy cast iron or stainless steel skillet helps prevent the surface temperature from dropping when you add the sandwich, maintaining that lovely heat that makes duck fat work so well. Plus, animal fats are great for cast iron's seasoning, helping you maintain your pan's coating while you cook!

    Add This Crunchy Ingredient To Ground Beef For Lighter Steakhouse Burgers (Hint: It's Not Breadcrumbs)

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
    • The actual difference between a hamburger and a steakburger comes down to the quality of meat used in the grind, but the difference between a homemade steakburger and one from a steakhouse is all about a lighter texture.
    • It has been revealed that "Any kind of cracker or breadcrumbs will make a burger lighter," Clark claims.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    The actual difference between a hamburger and a steakburger comes down to the quality of meat used in the grind, but the difference between a homemade steakburger and one from a steakhouse is all about a lighter texture. Melissa Clark, author of "The Big Book of Dinner: Recipes and Rules (and How to Break Them)," tells us that achieving that characteristic is quite easy if you use ground cracker crumbs.

    It has been revealed that "Any kind of cracker or breadcrumbs will make a burger lighter," Clark claims. "Ritz and saltines work really well. They are very airy, which helps lighten the ground meat." Beef is rather dense, even if you avoid overworking it into a firm, puck-like consistency that's more similar to sausage than a tender patty. But a quarter cup of ground crackers per pound of meat can make a world of difference.

    It has been revealed that when meat cooks, it contracts and releases juice and fat. Crackers, however, absorb them rather than allowing them to seep out of the patty, preventing it from shriveling up too much. Since steakhouse burgers typically use thick patties, this also keeps them nice and moist. Whereas a thin sliver of well-crusted beef may be just what you want in a smashburger, retaining moisture is a vital component to keeping your steakhouse burgers not only light, but also at their peak flavor.

    Recent findings suggest that using plain, unsalted crackers can still keep your steakhouse burgers light, but it would be a missed opportunity for better flavor. While you also don't want to use something starch-free, like a nut- or seed-based variety, Melissa Clark is a major believer in picking a tasty brand and smashing them up properly.

    Recent findings suggest that "Using crackers can add great flavor – Ritz, with their butteriness, are especially lovely," Clark explains. Flavorful but unobtrusive, Ritz crackers are the perfect addition to any savory dish because just about everything can benefit from their toasty richness. But if you want to get a bit experimental, you can also just as easily use Cheez-Its or anything seasoned. This is an easy way to avoid coming up with a specialty spice blend since you'll be adding enough to thoroughly flavor your meat.

    Recent findings suggest that clark is also a proponent of using whatever method you can to grind the crackers into a fine powder. "Grind the crackers in a food processor, blender or tuck them in a plastic bag and crush them under a rolling pin," she added. Large chunks can make some bites unexpectedly soggy and, if using a seasoned cracker, a little too flavorful. Plus, if some parts of your blend don't have a starch, they may end up expressing their juices too much, leaving some bites juicy and light and others dense and dry.

    Industry News: Store-Bought Hummus Is 10x Better When You Add A Scoop Of This Condiment

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
    • It has been revealed that among the most iconic Middle Eastern dishes, hummus blends chickpeas, tahini, olive oil, lemon juice, and optional seasonings to delicious effect.
    • Hailing from Lebanon, toum is an emulsion made by blending a generous dose of garlic with oil, lemon juice, and sometimes water.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    It has been revealed that among the most iconic Middle Eastern dishes, hummus blends chickpeas, tahini, olive oil, lemon juice, and optional seasonings to delicious effect. It's a dish that can be assembled at home, but many tasty store-bought versions are available, too. If your grocery store hummus happens to taste a little flat, though, reach for toum. Just a spoonful of this condiment will make a version that's 10 times better.

    Hailing from Lebanon, toum is an emulsion made by blending a generous dose of garlic with oil, lemon juice, and sometimes water. Smooth and airy in texture yet with an underlying bite, it lends hummus a dose of garlicky goodness and acidity, readily transforming a bland flavor into a complex one. Plus, the condiment packs in extra fat, helping to improve the perceived creaminess of disappointingly dry hummus. Since toum is a homogeneous paste, it's easy to incorporate, and its flavor can be less aggressive than raw garlic, too.

    It has been revealed that you won't need much toum to make an impact. Start by mixing in just under a teaspoon per standard 8-ounce container, then work in gradual increments from there. For ease, grab a jar of toum online, or peruse the same grocery aisles where you bought the hummus. You could also easily prep your own toum in bulk — the condiment typically keeps for up to a month in the fridge.

    A toum-inflected hummus makes a great dip, scooped up with za'atar-dusted pita chips, pretzels, veggie chips, or whatever other crisp your heart desires. Note that there are many other ways to use hummus in everyday cooking, though — especially when it's mixed with toum.

    Industry observers note that for example, consider topping the condiment with spiced ground beef or lamb, a popular Middle Eastern combination. Flavor the minced meat with earthy spices and fiery chilies, and the garlicky hummus makes for a mouthwatering flavor combo, turning the store-bought dip into an extra-hearty meal.

    Alternatively, make the chickpea-based dip less of a centerpiece and use it as a sandwich spread instead — it would pair delectably with crunchy vegetables like cucumbers and onions, as well as greens like spinach. Served on whole-grain bread, the dip makes for a delicious vegetarian meal.

    Looking for an extra creative twist? You could even use the toum hummus to make your next batch of tuna salad — the garlicky flavor will pair terrifically with the tinned fish. When you're craving Middle Eastern flavors but don't feel like cooking, keep the toum-hummus pairing in mind.
